title: procurement-tools spec-as-code
description: Machine-readable requirement set for one purchase or one market survey. Written as YAML (spec.yaml, or spec-<variant>.yaml when a spec has parallel variants), validated and rendered by scripts/spec_tools.py. Identity is the triple id + variant + revision: id names the purchase and is shared by every variant of it, variant names a parallel either/or branch (budget vs premium), and revision moves linearly within one variant. Requirement IDs are stable across BOTH revisions and variants, and are the join key used by conformance records, BOM lines and RFQ line items.

spec_version.description: Version of THIS file format, not of the spec. Currently 1.

id.description: Stable slug for the purchase, e.g. 'laser-measure-2026-08'. Shared by every variant of the same purchase — the variant field, not the id, is what distinguishes them. Referenced by conformance records and BOM lines.

variant.description: Slug naming a parallel either/or branch of this spec, e.g. 'budget' or 'premium'. OMIT ENTIRELY for the common case of a single spec with iterative revisions — an absent variant means the purchase has no variants, and the file is spec.yaml. When variants exist, every spec file in the workspace carries one and is named spec-<variant>.yaml; a bare spec.yaml must not survive alongside them, because it is then ambiguous which spec is in force.

variant_label.description: Human-readable name for the variant, used as the column header when variants are compared. Defaults to the variant slug.

variant_rationale.description: The trade-off this variant takes, in one sentence — 'cheapest thing that still clears the safety requirements', 'no compromise on throughput, accept 2x cost'. This is what a reader compares when choosing between variants, so it is required in practice once variant is set.

variant_of.description: The variant slug this one was branched from, for provenance. Absent on the first variant. Never a chain to walk at evaluation time — variants are siblings, not a hierarchy.

revision.description: Increments on every change that alters what would pass. Independent per variant: budget r3 and premium r1 are both current. Conformance records pin the variant and revision they were evaluated against, so a bump invalidates nothing silently.

status.description: frozen = no further changes while a purchase is in flight. superseded = a later spec replaces it; name it in supersedes_note.

scope.description: What is being specified, in capability terms. Vendor-neutral: no product may appear here.

out_of_scope.description: What this spec deliberately does NOT constrain. Load-bearing: it stops incidental attributes of an example product being promoted to requirements downstream.

destination.description: Address profile id, matching addresses.yaml used by price-scan.

id.description: Allocated sequentially and NEVER reused, even after retirement. Stable across variants as well as revisions: REQ-005 names the same SUBJECT in every variant of a spec (e.g. 'throughput'), even where the variants set different thresholds for it. That is what makes a cross-variant diff readable and lets one candidate be judged against several variants without re-researching it. A requirement that exists in only one variant simply does not appear in the others' lists. This is the join key across every other artefact.

title.description: Short column header for the matrix. Defaults to a truncation of the statement.

kind.description: must = disqualifying if absent. must-not = disqualifying if present. nice = tie-breaker, never disqualifies and never scores.

statement.description: The requirement in one sentence, phrased as a property of the product rather than of a purchase. Written so a subagent that has never seen this repo can judge it.

parameter.description: The measurable attribute, when there is one, e.g. 'bluetooth_profile', 'max_range', 'ip_rating'.

operator.description: Only meaningful alongside parameter. Makes the requirement checkable rather than arguable.

verify.description: The evidence class that SETTLES this requirement. Anything weaker leaves the cell unknown rather than passing it.

evidence.description: What specifically would settle it — the datasheet field, the manual section, the standard clause, the question to ask the vendor. This is the sentence a research subagent acts on.

rejects.description: Evidence that looks sufficient and is not. Retail bullet points, marketing copy, a spec repeated across roundups from one wrong original.

rationale.description: Why this is required. Read when deciding whether to relax it.

added_in.description: Spec revision this requirement first appeared in.

variant_note.description: Why this variant's threshold or kind differs from its siblings' for this same requirement id. Only meaningful when the spec has a variant. Read when converging variants back to one.

retired.description: Requirements are retired, never deleted, so historic conformance records stay interpretable.
